title: Immutable exports, restore and cross-tenant sharing for calibration runs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce immutable export bundles for calibration runs (FP8/INT8), a deterministic restore workflow, and controlled cross-tenant sharing to enable reproducible quantization validation and safe artifact movement between workspaces.
background: Teams run large calibration sweeps that produce quant-profiles, histograms, and eval traces. Customers need a way to export run artifacts immutably for audit, offline validation, or to migrate to Dedicated/Private deployments. Current export is ad-hoc and editable in place, leading to divergence between what was validated and what was served.
goals: 1) Produce signed, immutable export bundles for calibration runs; 2) Implement restore/import that preserves provenance and validation metadata; 3) Add cross-tenant share capability with ACLs and expiry; 4) Ensure exports comply with retention and TTL policies and integrate with console audit logs.
non_goals: 1) Full multi-region replication of artifacts (out of scope for MVP); 2) Implementing binary deduplication across tenants; 3) Automatic re-calibration on import (import will be read-only by default).
success_metrics: Number of exported bundles created per week > 20 for enterprise customers
Reduction in support tickets related to ‘missing calibration artifact’ by 75%
100% of exported bundles have verifiable provenance metadata and signature
proposed_design: Exports are produced as a single signed bundle (.rbc) containing: quant-profile artifacts, per-layer histograms, sample evaluation traces, the prompt/eval corpus hash, the calibration config, and a provenance manifest. Bundles are content-addressed and immutable once created. Restore imports create a read-only calibration run replica in the target workspace while preserving original run_id and provenance metadata with an import record linked to the actor.
ux_notes: Add an 'Export bundle' CTA on run detail. Export modal shows scope (full run vs subset), bundle size estimate, expiry TTL for share links, and required approvals for cross-tenant exports. Import flow warns about mismatch between runtime model versions and suggests compatible quant-profile variants.
infra_requirements: S3-compatible storage with object-lock or versioning enabled for signed bundles, KMS integration for signing keys, new provenance index in metadata DB, and background job to garbage-collect expired share links respecting retention policy.
data_migration_plan: Backfill provenance for existing historical runs by running a one-time scanner that computes manifest hashes and signs bundles for runs flagged by customers. Provide a migration toggle for customers to opt into historic export creation to avoid spikes.
retention_policy_spec: Exports inherit the run's retention tier but are stored as immutable artifacts with separate TTL controls. Default: 365 days for enterprise, 90 days for self-serve. Admins can set per-organization TTLs. Deletion requires dual-approval and is recorded in audit logs.
permission_matrix: Creators and workspace admins can create exports. Cross-tenant share requires 'export:share' role and an approval workflow for P0 customers. Imports create read-only replicas unless importer has 'import:write' to allow promotion. All actions emit audit events with actor, timestamp, and source IP.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): in-console export/import for same-tenant and signed bundles (limited beta), Phase 2: cross-tenant share and link expiry, Phase 3: enterprise policies (dual-approval, custom TTLs) and CLI/SDK support. Start with 10 pilot customers before broad GA.
monitoring_and_alerting: Track export creation success/failure rate, bundle signing latency, failed import attempts, and number of expired share links. Alert on signing key rotation failure, and storage fill >= 80%.
qa_plan: Test scenarios: export round-trip (export -> import -> verify artifact hash), cross-tenant share with ACLs, expired-link rejection, restore provenance integrity, failure injection for partial bundle upload, storage permission rollback tests.
open_questions: Should exported bundles be encrypted per-tenant by default?
Do we allow exporters to redact sample traces before export?
What is the expected max bundle size for pilots and do we require chunking?
decisions: Use KMS-backed digital signatures for bundle provenance
Exports are immutable once written; deletion requires dual-approval
Imported runs are read-only by default to guarantee reproducibility
notes: 2026-02-18: Initial draft and scope laid out. 2026-02-25: Security reviewed approach for signatures; requested KMS integration. 2026-03-03: Design feedback - include explicit read-only import behavior. 2026-03-10: SRE highlighted storage object-lock requirement and GC implications. 2026-03-14: PM aligned pilot customer list and prioritized dual-approval requirement for deletion.
next_steps: 1) Kickoff with Eng and Security to define signing key lifecycle; 2) Design prototype export bundle manifest and schema; 3) Implement storage and signing PoC; 4) Prepare pilot onboarding checklist and runbook.
